permanent_palette_split.XD: Every live X-type and D-type vertex has exact palette contained in {1,2}; the seed U-type vertices h1_1=3 and h1_6=4 are complete to all X/D vertices and remain fixed.
permanent_palette_split.U: Every live U-type vertex has exact palette contained in {3,4}; the permanent fixed X/D vertices d2=1 and ~x2=2 are complete to every U-type vertex.
permanent_palette_split.persistence: Authorized B2B1 forcing only adds fixed colors and cannot destroy this separation.

local_clause_carrier.boundary_state: For each variable occurrence use p_i=(col(x_i),col(d_i)) in P={(1,1),(1,2),(2,1),(2,2)}; ~x_i is determined oppositely whenever live.
local_clause_carrier.local_future_state: A C7 clause may have any proper partial precoloring of its three C-type and four U-type internal vertices consistent with the permanent side palettes.
local_clause_carrier.exact_factorization: For every extendable local future state, its boundary relation R on P^3 has the exact form R=(D1 x D2 x D3) intersect eq^{-1}(M), where Dt subseteq P is unary and M subseteq {0,1}^3 is coordinatewise upward-closed.
local_clause_carrier.root_relation: With no internal clause precoloring, M={0,1}^3 minus {(0,0,0)}; equivalently e1 OR e2 OR e3.

global_carrier.variable_domain: For each variable i store the four-state domain D_i subseteq P obtained by intersecting direct/fixed restrictions and every incident clause unary factor.
global_carrier.clause_state: For every clause store its constant-size upward relation M_j and a constant witness table for allowed boundary tuples.
global_carrier.maximal_equality_assignment: Define e_i^max=1 iff D_i contains an equal pair state, otherwise 0. Since every M_j is upward-closed, the whole current future state is feasible iff every D_i is nonempty and, for every clause j=(a,b,c), (e_a^max,e_b^max,e_c^max) belongs to M_j.
global_carrier.soundness: Any feasible assignment has equality vector coordinatewise <= e^max. Upward closure implies that if some feasible vector satisfies all clauses then e^max does as well.
global_carrier.completeness: If e^max satisfies all clause relations, choose independently for each variable any state in D_i with equality bit e_i^max; exact local factorization then admits every clause, and stored local witnesses reconstruct its C/U colors.
global_carrier.reconstruction: Set ~x_i to the opposite color of x_i where applicable, use stored clause witnesses, then append B2B1 deleted-component receipts and fixed identity-color ledger.

R1_R2.R1: Restrict the appropriate variable four-state domain or add one local C/U precolor, rebuild the affected local relation(s), and run the maximal-equality feasibility test.
R1_R2.R2: Apply both same-color restrictions simultaneously; common color is a constant label. Then run the same carrier.
R1_R2.successful_update: After an authorized successful force, invoke sealed B2B1 canonical return and rebuild this carrier from the resulting fixed/active statuses. No recursive R1/R2 assumption is used.

complexity.carrier_size: O(number_of_variables + number_of_clauses) words plus fixed/reconstruction ledgers; for the sealed H_k family this is O(|G_k|).
complexity.rebuild: polynomial; a full rebuild scans variables, clause gadgets and incidence once up to constant local work
complexity.R1_R2_query: polynomial by one temporary restriction plus rebuild/local update and the maximal-equality test
complexity.reconstruction: polynomial using one local constant witness per clause plus variable/fixed/deleted receipts

interpretation.E3_profiles: The 2^k E3 canonical profiles remain real and may be domain-aware distinct, but they have an exact polynomial future-behavior carrier.
interpretation.new_principle: Even E2-uncovered four-color-active connected profile multiplicity need not imply hard exact future representation.

gate_verdict.E2_addendum_required: YES: add an exact BINARY_PAIR_UPWARD_EQUALITY_CSP carrier as C10 before later stress promotion.

explicit_nonclaims: No polynomial carrier theorem for arbitrary connected Q_ALL.
No hardness conclusion from Huang's NP-hardness theorem.
